45218.subject: Government
45218.question_text: Government refers to all the following except
45218.explanation:
Government typically refers to:

  • An academic field of study: The study of government and political systems is a recognized academic discipline.
  • An organised group of people that formulate policies: This describes how government functions, with organised groups (such as branches or departments) responsible for policy-making.
  • A process of making and enforcing laws: Government involves the creation and enforcement of laws to maintain order and regulate society.

An institution made up of people with common interests, however, refers to organisations or groups that might not be governmental but are focused on shared goals or interests, such as clubs, societies, or special interest groups. These are not necessarily involved in the formal processes of governance.

options.text: an organized group of people that formulate policies
a process of making and enforcing laws
an institution made up of people with common interest

45219.subject: Government
45219.question_text: All the following are experienced by a community without government except
45219.explanation:
In a community without government, issues such as insecurity, lawlessness and political anarchy are commonly experienced due to the absence of organised structures to maintain order, enforce laws and provide security. However, planned development is not experienced in such a community.

Planned development requires structured governance to create and implement development plans and policies. Without a government, there is usually no organised mechanism for planning and executing development projects.

45220.subject: Government
45220.question_text: As an academic field the study of government does not include
45220.explanation: Government as an academic field of study:- is the study of political institutions and theories, which deals with the acquisition and use of political power. It is a social science subject taught in higher institution.

45222.subject: Government
45222.question_text: Which of the following systems of government is authoritarian in nature?
45222.explanation:
Fascism is a form of far right-wing, authoritarian ultranationalism characterized by dictatorial power, forcible suppression of opposition, and strong regimentation of society and of the economy 

Fascism is a form of government which is a type of one-party dictatorship. Fascistsare against democracy. ... Fascism puts nation and often race above the individual. It stands for a centralized government headed by a dictator.

45224.subject: Government
45224.question_text: The system that allows the opposition to participate in governance is
45224.explanation: In a democratic country, all eligible citizens have the right to participate, either directly or indirectly, in making the decisions that affect them. It also allows the participation of the opposition in governance

45226.subject: Government
45226.question_text: Which of the following hinders the establishment of a representative government in a state?
45226.explanation: Illiteracy is a state whereby one is unable to read and write. In its simplest form, it can be defined as lack of any or sufficient education. Sometimes people who have had very basic education also experience challenges in reading and writing. When majority of the electorates are illiterates, electoral malpractice prevalent, making  representative government difficult

45227.subject: Government
45227.question_text: Which of the following is not an attribute of a state?
45227.explanation: The state has four essential attributes, Population, Territory, Government and Sovereignty. Population and territory constitute the physical basis of the State while government and sovereignty constitute its legal basis or political basis.

45229.subject: Government
45229.question_text: In a democracy political sovereignty is vested in the
45229.explanation: Popular sovereignty is the principle that the authority of a state and its government are created and sustained by the consent of its people, through their elected representatives (Rule by the People), who is the source of all political power.

45230.subject: Government
45230.question_text: According to Charles Montesquieu, the theory of separation of powers is to prevent
45230.explanation:
Baron de Montesquieu in in his book titled '' The Spirit of the Laws, argued for a constitutional government with three separate branches, each of which would have defined abilities to check the powers of the others. This is to prevent cases like arbitrariness.

Arbitrariness is the quality of being based on random choice or personal whim, rather than any reason or system.

45232.subject: Government
45232.explanation: Decentralization—the transfer of authority and responsibility for public functions from the central government to subordinate or quasi-independent government organizations. The governmental powers in a federal system of government is decentralized in a way that, authority and reponsibilities are shared among the federal, state and local government .

45234.subject: Government
45234.explanation:
Delegated legislation means the exercise of legislative power by an agency that is subordinate to the legislature.

Not all laws are made by the government. Some Acts of Parliament give other organisations the power to make laws– usually local councils.

45235.subject: Government
45235.question_text: Power is transformed into legal authority through
45235.explanation: Legitimacy is a political concept which refers to the acceptance and recognition by the citizens of a country the right of their rulers to govern. Power is  transformed into legal authority by legitimizing it.

45237.subject: Government
45237.question_text: Conventions are mostly used by states that have
45237.explanation: Conventions are mostly used by states that have an unwritten constitution. In such states, conventions are established practices or norms that are not formally codified in written law but are followed as part of the political system. These conventions help guide the functioning of government and fill gaps where the Constitution is silent.

options.text: a lot of people not interested in political activities

45260.subject: Government
45260.question_text: One advantage of a flexible constitution is that it
45260.explanation:
1. A flexible constitution can be amended with the same ease and facility with which ordinary laws are altered. (with a simple majority voting in favor of its amendment)

2.  A flexible constitution can easily adopt the needs of people with the change of time because of its elasticity.

3. A flexible constitution is very useful for developing a country, because it is a great expression of its development. It does not hinder progress due to it's adaptability. 

4. Flexible constitution is moulded by the conventions of national life.

options.text: is best suited for a federation
can be amended by a simple majority

45262.subject: Government
45262.question_text: A constitution that requires complicated procedure for its amendment is
45262.explanation: Rigid constitution is  a constitution that is difficult or slow to change usually because of a prescribed process of amendment that is detailed and lengthy

45263.subject: Government
45263.question_text: The official who enforces discipline among members of his party in parliament is the
45263.explanation: The Chief Whip is a political office in some legislatures whose task is to administer the whipping system that tries to ensure that members of the party attend and vote as the party leadership desires.

45265.subject: Government
45265.question_text: When an action of the executive is declared ultra-vires, it is a control exercised by the
45265.explanation: Ultra-vires means acting or done beyond one's legal power or authority.

45269.subject: Government
45269.question_text: In a presidential system of government, the president can constitutionally be removed from the office through
45269.explanation: Impeachment is the process by which a legislative body levels charges against a government official. it is one of the ways a president can be removed  from office

45270.subject: Government
45270.question_text: One of the features of an absolute monarch is that the ruler
45270.explanation: Absolute monarchy, or absolutism, meant that the ultimate authority to run a state was in the hands of a king who ruled by divine right.

options.text: has a definite tenure of office
is elected by the representatives of the people
wields the supreme power in a state

45272.subject: Government
45272.question_text: A notable feature of cabinet system of government is
45272.explanation: The most distinctive characteristic of a Cabinet system of government is the complete and continuous responsibility of the executive to the legislature. Collectively, the Cabinet shapes the programme of legislation which is submitted to Parliament and from it emanates the broad and general policies.

45273.subject: Government
45273.question_text: All the following are the conditions for the adoption of federalism except
45273.explanation:
Different groups within a country may adopt federalism as a means of preventing the over-concentration of power at the centre. This is one way in which they can prevent the country from drifting into dictatorship. States with a common historical background can come together to form a federation.

Homogeneity is the quality or state of being all the same or all of the same kind.

45275.subject: Government
45275.question_text: The privileged citizens enjoyed in a country irrespective of sex, tribe or creed is
45275.explanation: The rights belonging to an individual by virtue of citizenship, including civil liberties, due process, equal protection of the laws, and freedom from discrimination.

45276.subject: Government
45276.question_text: The judicial order requiring a detained person to be brought before a judge is the writ of
45276.explanation: Habeas corpus; is a writ requiring a person under arrest to be brought before a judge or into court, especially to secure the person's release unless lawful grounds are shown for their detention.

45279.subject: Government
45279.question_text: A political party can contest and win a widely accepted election if it has
45279.explanation: A political party can win a widely accepted election when it has a broad / wide base of  members and supporters who will vote for the party during elections.

options.text: the support of very wealthy politicians

45283.subject: Government
45283.question_text: Political parties aim at all the following except
45283.explanation: Party members in each branch suggest ideas for party policies. They help choose, or pre-select, party candidates for local, state and federal elections. They also assist with election campaigns, distribute 'how to vote' cards on Election Day, and help scrutinise the counting of votes.

45286.subject: Government
45286.question_text: Which of the following is not a means through which political parties reach the populace?
45286.explanation:
Political parties typically use various means to reach the populace, including:

  • Posters: Used for visual communication and advertising in public spaces.
  • Newspapers: Provide news coverage and articles that can be used to convey political messages and party platforms.
  • The internet: Offers a wide range of digital platforms (websites, social media) for engaging with voters and sharing information.

Schools, however, are not used by political parties as a direct means of reaching the populace. While educational institutions may indirectly influence public opinion through education, they are not a primary medium for political campaigning or outreach.

45288.subject: Government
45288.question_text: An association whose ultimate aim is to influence government policies is known as
45288.explanation: Pressure group is a group that tries to influence government / public policy in the interest of a particular cause.

45291.subject: Government
45291.question_text: Membership of pressure groups is usually limited because they
45291.explanation: Pressure groups often have limited membership because they focus on specific and narrow objectives. These groups are formed around particular issues or causes, and their appeal may be limited to individuals who are particularly interested in or affected by those issues. This focus helps them to concentrate their efforts and resources effectively, but it also means that their membership base tends to be smaller and more specialised compared to broader organizations.

options.text: promote the interest of the government

45296.subject: Government
45296.explanation: The nature of democracy is that elected officials are accountable to the people, and they must return to the voters at prescribed intervals to seek their mandate to continue in office. Election ensures the citizens choose their preferred candidates to represent them at various elective position

options.text: provide permanent employment for the people
make the people choose their leaders
known the number of people in a country
know the social amenities in the community

45299.subject: Government
45299.explanation: Suffrage is the right to vote in political elections. It is also known as franchise

45301.subject: Government
45301.question_text: For an election to be fair and free Electoral Commission must be
45301.explanation: An independent electoral commission ensures the conduct of free, fair and credible elections

options.text: headed by a minister in the executive
independent of other institutions of government

45303.subject: Government
45303.question_text: Which of the following categories of people can vote in periodic elections?
45303.explanation:
The following are some of the requirements for voting in an election;

  • Must be a citizen of that country. 
  • At least 18 years of age on or before the date of the next election.
  • A current resident of that country/state
  • Not in prison or on parole for a felony conviction.

45304.subject: Government
45304.question_text: The anonymity of a civil servant means that he
45304.explanation: The anonymity of the civil service is linked to two concepts: permanence and neutrality. Civil servants, many of whom remain in their jobs whilst serving numerous governments, are thus likely to have to give advice to governments of different political parties, who may have different attitudes to policy. The advice they give needs to be given to ministers both freely and also without fear of adverse public or political reactions and without fear of future career damage.

options.text: is above the law of the land
should take part in partisan politics
receives neither praise nor blame publicly
should be prosecuted for professional misconduct

45306.subject: Government
45306.question_text: Which of the following functions is performed by the civil service?
45306.explanation: The Civil service is the entity that is charged with the responsibility of carrying out government policies, providing services to the public and keeping the machinery of government running. One of the functions of the Civil Service is to implement the policies of the government of the day.

45310.subject: Government
45310.explanation: One of the major  reason for establishment of Public Corporation is to lower the prices of the goods and services they provide.

options.text: provide utility services to the public at minimal cost

45311.subject: Government
45311.explanation: A minister's role with a public corporation is to oversee and ensure the effective administration of the corporation.

options.text: auditing the accounts of the corporation personally
criticizing the corporation through the mass media
ensuring the effective administration of the corporation

45312.subject: Government
45312.question_text: An institution of government that makes bye-laws is the
45312.explanation: A byelaw is a law which is made by a body, such as a local authority, under an enabling power established by an Act of Parliament and which has been confirmed by the Secretary of State.

45313.subject: Government
45313.explanation: Local government brings about grass root inclusion and development. A grassroots movement is one which uses the people in a given district, region, or community as the basis for a political or economic movement.

options.text: give more powers to the traditional rulers
bring the government closer to the people
make the people obey more of the local laws
take over the functions of the central government

45314.subject: Government
45314.question_text: Some pre-colonial West African governments were democratic because of the existence of
45314.explanation: In pre-colonial West Africa, some governance systems exhibited democratic features due to their internal mechanisms of checks and balances. These mechanisms ensured that power was not concentrated in the hands of a single individual or group. Instead, various institutions or councils had specific roles and powers that balanced each other.

45315.subject: Government
45315.question_text: One of the measures introduced by indirect rule was
45315.explanation: Educated elites were excluded in the administration of the colonial indirect rule system

options.text: collection and keeping of taxes by the chiefs only
fixing and collection of taxes by British officials themselves
exclusion of the educated elite from the colonial administration

45316.subject: Government
45316.question_text: Which of the following policies was replaced by the French Policy of Association?
45316.explanation: The assimilation policy was a policy of absorbing Aboriginal people into white society through the process of removing children from their families. The ultimate intent of this policy was the destruction of Aboriginal society.

45317.subject: Government
45317.question_text: The appointment and deposition of chiefs by their people was a demand of the
45317.explanation: The National Congress of British West Africa (NCBWA) was a significant Pan-African and nationalist organization founded in 1944. It sought to address various issues affecting West Africa under colonial rule, including the political and social rights of the people. One of its key demands was for greater local control and autonomy, which included the appointment and deposition of chiefs by their own communities rather than by colonial authorities.

options.text: National Congress of British West Africa

45318.subject: Government
45318.question_text: The desire for constitutional development in British West African Colonies was as a result of the
45318.explanation: The desire for constitutional development in British West African colonies stemmed primarily from the growing agitation of the people for political independence. As the people became more aware of their rights and the need for self-governance, they increasingly demanded reforms and constitutional changes that would lead to greater autonomy and eventual independence from British colonial rule. This movement was driven by educated elites, nationalists, and other groups pushing for political and social reforms.

options.text: desire of the British to review the constitution
power of traditional rulers in British West Africa
growing agitation of the people for political independence

45319.subject: Government
45319.question_text: The following are features of military regimes except
45319.explanation: Military regimes are often characterised by suspension of the constitution, rule by decrees and edicts and curtailment of human rights. However, they are not typically associated with respect for human rights. Instead, military governments tend to prioritise control and order at the expense of individual freedoms and rights.

45320.subject: Government
45320.question_text: Military regimes in West Africa have often made use of civilians because
45320.explanation: Military regimes in West Africa have often included civilians in their governments because civilians possess the necessary experience, expertise and knowledge of governance that military officers typically lack. While military officers may have control over the armed forces and security, civilians are often more familiar with the complexities of administration, law, economics and other aspects of government.

options.text: civilians are part of the armed forces
they need the experience of civilians in government

45321.subject: Government
45321.question_text: One criticism levelled against the pre-independence political parties in West Africa was that some of them
45321.explanation: One major criticism of the pre-independence political parties in West Africa was that they often lacked a national outlook. This means that many of these parties were regionally or ethnically based, focusing on the interests of specific groups rather than representing the entire nation. This lack of a national perspective hindered their ability to unify the country and build a broad-based political movement that could effectively challenge colonial rule and promote national independence.

options.text: did not contribute to political development
were instruments of the colonial administration

45322.subject: Government
45322.explanation: Foreign policy is simply a government's strategy in dealing with other nations.

options.text: general principles that guide foreigners in a country
policy made by a country during war
policy made by a country in peace time
general principles of a country in the conduct of international relations

45323.subject: Government
45323.question_text: The Commonwealth of Nations was originally made up of
45323.explanation: The Commonwealth was first officially formed in 1926 when the Balfour Declaration of the Imperial Conference recognized the full sovereignty of dominions. Known as the "British Commonwealth", the original members were the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, Irish Free State, and Newfoundland.

options.text: independent nations formerly under British Empire
France and her former colonies in West Africa

45324.subject: Government
45324.question_text: Which of the following countries was not instrumental to the formation of the United Nations Organization (UNO)?
45324.explanation: The United Nations Organization (UNO) was established in 1945 after World War II to promote peace, security and cooperation among nations. The founding members included the United States of America, Britain, the USSR, and many other countries. Germany was not instrumental in the formation of the UNO because it was one of the defeated Axis powers in World War II and was not involved in the initial establishment of the organisation.
